rationale: Proper-noun run matcher. Separator (\s+) is disjoint from the word class ([A-Za-z0-9]), so decomposition is unambiguous and backtracking is already linear (verified <0.4ms on 60KB adversarial). Hardened by capping each word token to 64 chars ({0,63} after the leading cap) and the phrase to 16 words ({0,15}), bounding worst-case work and clearing the nested-quantifier scanner flag. Real proper nouns fit comfortably.

nrg triple-value reader. The quoted branch (?:[^"\]|\.)* is the Friedl unrolled-loop form: its two alternatives are mutually exclusive on the first char (non-backslash vs backslash), so it is NOT catastrophic (verified <4ms on a 60KB unterminated quote). Hardened by bounding the quoted body ({0,4096}) and the bare token ({1,4096}). SEPARATE latent issue for the source PR: {key} is interpolated UN-escaped here (its sibling check_neurosymbolic_repo_graph_ttl_fixtures.py uses re.escape) — wrap with re.escape(key) to prevent regex-injection if key ever becomes non-literal.

Reverse-DNS app id (REVDNS, flags i). Separator is a literal \. disjoint from the label class, so partitioning is unique and backtracking linear. Anchored already; hardened with DNS-realistic caps: each label <=63 chars, <=11 labels total. Anchored length caps let the engine fail fast (worst-adv dropped to ~0ms).

DOMAIN_RE (breach_lookup). risk_class catastrophic by rubric but structurally linear: the literal-dot separator makes label partition unique (verified ~0.1ms). Hardened with DNS caps: label <=63 chars, <=10 dotted labels, TLD 2-24 chars — bounds work and rejects absurd inputs early.

Capitalized-run entity matcher (schema.ts, flags g). Repetition already bounded {1,4}; separator [ -] disjoint from [a-zA-Z.]. Hardened by capping each word token to 64 chars so a single 60KB token cannot drive linear-but-large work.

Device-service metric name (JSON Schema pattern, two sites). Literal-dot separator, unique partition, linear. Hardened with per-segment cap (<=64 chars) and <=16 segments. NOTE: this is a JSON Schema "pattern" consumed by the schema validator; the source fix is a schema edit, and the caps must stay ECMA-262-compatible (they are).

OCW 'Prof. <Name>' footer stripper (mmlu-brain-bench.ts, flags gim). Repetition bounded {0,2}. Hardened two ways: (a) cap each name token to 64 chars; (b) replace \s+ with [ \t]+ — under the m flag \s also matches \n, which both risks crossing line boundaries on a per-line footer strip AND was the one spot where the inner \s+ overlapped the trailing [ \t]*$ boundary. [ \t]+ removes that overlap and keeps the strip line-local. Verified valid inputs (incl. 'Professor Jane A. Doe', 'Prof. Jean-Luc Picard') still match.
METRIC_ID (validate_standards.py). Literal-dot separator, unique partition, linear. Hardened with per-segment cap (<=64) and <=16 segments; anchored fail-fast.

nrg reader (check_neurosymbolic fixtures). Same Friedl unrolled quote body as rx-2cb1bdd5a3 (mutually-exclusive alternatives, non-catastrophic, verified <4ms). Already uses re.escape(predicate) (good). Hardened by bounding quoted body ({0,4096}) and bare token ({1,4096}).

PY_JOIN path-literal matcher (check_workflow_path_filters.py). Quoted segments are delimited so partition is unique; linear. Hardened by capping each quoted segment body to 256 chars and the segment chain to 33 ({0,32}+1). (Latent non-ReDoS nit for the source PR: ["'] open can be closed by the other quote type; a backreferenced quote (?P<q>["'])...(?P=q) would tighten correctness but is out of scope for the ReDoS fix.)
